deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics: no formulas, computations or derivations. It is a short philosophical draft, continuing the 'Causalität' fragment on the previous page (fol. 97r). The previous page set out these theses. (I) What an agens strives to bring about must be fixed by the concept of the agens alone, so its action depends only on its own nature. (II) This demand is met only if the agens strives to preserve or restore itself. (III) Hence agentia must be states of things or relations between things, not things, and they must admit degrees of deviation. (IV) Which things they act on cannot be fixed by the concept of the agens. That page ended with remarks on Kant and Hume.

This page turns to the history of the principle.

(1) A struck-through opening: roughly 'In the newer philosophy the principle [that the action of a thing depends only on its own nature] played an important role.' It was rewritten as 'spielte der Satz ... eine wichtige Rolle.'

(2) 'Every essential epoch of philosophy has recognised the validity of the demand we have placed first [ihr vorausgestellten Forderung]...' The end of the line is illegible.

(3) My tentative reading of the image: '[Leibniz] wurde lediglich durch den Satz, daß die Action eines Wesens nur von seiner eigenen Natur abhängen könne, zu seiner Monadenlehre geführt.' In English: Leibniz was led to his monadology by the principle that a being's action can depend only on its own nature.

(4) A separate underlined heading: 'Aber dadurch wird die Natur [nicht?] erklärt' ('But this does [not?] explain nature'). This appears to object that the Leibnizian solution, self-contained monads without real interaction, does not account for natural interaction.

(5) Two trial formulations of a positive alternative. First: '[Impetus?], wenn er Widerstand findet, verwandelt sich in ein Streben ...' Second: '[Impetus?] verwandelt sich in Streben durch Widerstand.' That is, a motion or activity that meets resistance turns into a striving (conatus/tension).

The point serves the programme of the surrounding pages. Agentia are self-preserving or self-restoring states that, when obstructed, persist as striving, i.e. tension. This prepares Riemann's view of forces as states striving to restore themselves. That view appears in his published 'Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie' and other philosophical fragments in the Werke.

There is nothing to compute or check mathematically.

results.what: Principle that an agent's action is determined solely by its own concept/nature, so agents must be self-preserving or self-restoring states or relations rather than things. This page adds a historical note (Leibniz's monadology) and the idea that motion meeting resistance becomes striving.
results.modern_name: Leibnizian principle of spontaneity / conatus; dynamical theory of force as tendency to restore a state
results.usually_credited_to: Leibniz (Monadologie, 1714; conatus/impetus in Specimen dynamicum, 1695); Herbart's influence on Riemann

deep.surprise_reason: This is a purely philosophical draft fragment with no mathematical content. It fits Riemann's known Naturphilosophie and Herbart-influenced fragments, which are partly published in the Werke ('Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts'). Mentioning Leibniz's monadology and 'Streben durch Widerstand' is consistent with his known views.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'Ursprünglich wurde dadurch durch den Satz, daß die Natur einen Wechsel aus seiner eigenen Natur abhängen ... zu seiner Wanderung geführt' more plausibly reads 'Leibnitz wurde lediglich durch den Satz, daß die Action eines Wesens nur von seiner eigenen Natur abhängen könne, zu seiner Monadenlehre geführt' (tentative). The word read as 'Wanderung' matches 'Monadenlehre' in shape and context.

Line 1: the opening should likely be read as 'In der neueren Philosophie spielte der Satz ... eine wichtige Rolle', with the beginning struck through. The middle words are uncertain, probably a restatement of the principle about action depending on the agent's own nature.
Line 2: 'von uns ihr vorausgestellten' — 'ihr' is an interlinear insertion above 'vorausgestellten', and 'von uns' may be struck. The line ends with a struck-through phrase.

Lines 5–6: the first word read as 'Ursprünglich' / 'Ihm' is uncertain. It possibly reads 'Impetus' or 'Impuls' (struck in the first line, underlined in the second), giving 'Impetus verwandelt sich in Streben durch Widerstand'.
Line 4 (underlined heading): possibly 'Aber dadurch wird die Natur nicht erklärt' rather than 'erst erklärt' (uncertain).
